```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.2, message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE)
```

`GiVAE()` is an identifiable variational autoencoder whose latent components
depend on their neighbours in one or several graphs. The prior mean of a
latent component is a weighted average of the neighbours' encoded values,

$$\mu_i = \rho_{\max}\,\rho(u_i)\sum_{g=1}^{G}\beta_g(u_i)\,
\frac{1}{|\partial_g i|}\sum_{j\in\partial_g i}\hat z_j ,$$

where $\hat z_j$ is the encoder mean of neighbour $j$, $\rho(u_i)$ is the total
coupling strength and $\beta_g(u_i)$ shares it between the graphs. The prior
variance $\sigma^2(u_i)$ is nonstationary, which makes the model identifiable.
All three are neural networks of the auxiliary variables $u_i$, here the
eigenvectors of the graph Laplacians.

This example has two graphs: the adjacency graph of areal units, and a
directed graph of the time axis in which each time point has the previous one
as its only neighbour (like an AR(1) model).

## Data

```{r data}
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(NonlinearBSS)

areal <- generate_areal_units(n_area = 400, n_fine = 600,
                              seed_type = "uniform", seed = 1)
n_area <- nrow(areal$W)
n_time <- 200

src <- simulate_sources_areal(p = 5, areal = areal, n_time = n_time,
                              n_segments_time = 10, sd_range = c(0.4, 0.4),
                              nonstat_dependence = TRUE, basis = "laplacian",
                              nonstat_dependence_time = TRUE,
                              ar_range = c(0, 0), beta_s_range = c(0.01, 0.99), seed = 3)
x <- mix_data(src$sources, n_layers = 2, nonlinearity = "xtanh", normalize = FALSE)
```

The rows are ordered with the areal unit varying fastest within each time
point, so row $r$ is unit `(r - 1) %% n_area + 1` at time
`(r - 1) %/% n_area + 1`.

## Graphs

A graph has its own nodes, and `each` tells how they are repeated over the
rows. The spatial graph has `n_area` nodes and is repeated as a whole for every
time point (`each = 1`). The time graph has `n_time` nodes and every node is
repeated `n_area` times in a row (`each = n_area`). Neighbours are always
searched in the same context: the neighbours of unit $s$ at time $t$ in the
spatial graph are the adjacent units at time $t$, and in the time graph the
same unit $s$ at time $t - 1$.

```{r graphs}
g_space <- nlbss_graph(areal$W, name = "space")
g_time  <- nlbss_time_graph(n_time, each = n_area, lags = 1, directed = TRUE)
g_space
g_time
```

For other layouts `each` is the number of consecutive rows that share a node.
A graph with one node per observation uses `each = 1` and no repetition, and
for unsorted or incomplete data the node and the context of each row can be
given explicitly with `node` and `context` (see the last section).

## Auxiliary variables

By default `GiVAE()` uses the smoothest non-trivial Laplacian eigenvectors of
each graph, expanded to the rows with the graph's layout. They can also be used
with the other methods, e.g. in `iVAE()`.

```{r aux}
aux <- aux_laplacian(list(g_space, g_time), K = c(20L, 10L))
A <- aux_matrix(aux, matrix(0, nrow(x), 0))
dim(A)
```

The first three spatial eigenvectors are

```{r aux-plot}
plot_areal <- function(values, labels, fill = "value") {
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(values)), function(k) {
    d <- areal$areas_sf
    d$value <- values[, k]
    d$component <- labels[k]
    d[, c("value", "component")]
  }))
  long$component <- factor(long$component, levels = labels)
  ggplot(long) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = value), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~ component, ncol = length(labels)) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c() +
    coord_sf(datum = NA) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank()) +
    labs(fill = fill)
}
plot_areal(A[seq_len(n_area), 1:3], paste("Eigenvector", 1:3))
```

The first three temporal eigenvectors are the next block of columns after the
spatial ones. We take one representative row for each time point (the first
area in each time block), since the graph is repeated over all areas within a
single time point.

```{r aux-plot-time}
plot_time <- function(values, labels, fill = "value") {
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(values)), function(k) {
    d <- data.frame(
      time = seq_len(nrow(values)),
      value = values[, k],
      component = labels[k]
    )
    d
  }))
  long$component <- factor(long$component, levels = labels)
  ggplot(long, aes(x = time, y = value)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~ component, ncol = length(labels)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "time", y = "value", fill = fill)
}
space_cols <- 1:3
# the temporal block starts after the spatial block of eigenvectors
# (here: K = c(20, 20))
time_cols <- (aux$K[1] + 1L):(aux$K[1] + 4L)
time_rows <- (seq_len(n_time) - 1L) * n_area + 1L
plot_time(A[time_rows, time_cols], paste("Eigenvector", 1:3))
```

Plot generated latent components:

```{r latent-spat-plot}
plot_areal(src$sources[1:n_area, 1:3], paste("Latent Component ", 1:3))

W_row <- areal$W / rowSums(areal$W)
loc <- sapply(1:3, function(j) {
  Z <- matrix(src$sources[, j], n_area, n_time)   # area x time
  nb <- W_row %*% Z
  sapply(seq_len(n_area), function(i) cor(Z[i, ], nb[i, ]))
})
plot_areal(src$beta_s[, 1:3], paste("True beta", 1:3))
plot_areal(loc, paste("Estimated local dependence", 1:3))
cor(loc[, 1], src$beta_s[, 1])    # should be high
```

## Fitting GiVAE

For comparison, `iVAE()` gets the same auxiliary variables but no graph prior,
so it treats the rows as independent given $u$.

```{r fit, eval = tf_available()}
fit_ivae <- iVAEar(x, aux = aux, time = rep(1:n_time, each = n_area), 
                   group = rep(1:n_area, times = n_time), latent_dim = 5, 
                   epochs = 60, batch_size = 64,
                   verbose = 1, seed = 1, lr_end = 0.001)
fit_givae <- GiVAE(x, graphs = list(g_space, g_time), K = c(20L, 20L),
                   latent_dim = 5, epochs = 60, batch_size = 64, jacobian = "exact",
                   verbose = 1, seed = 1, error_dist_sigma = 0.01, lr_end = 0.001)
absolute_mean_correlation(fastICA::fastICA(x, 5)$S, src$sources)

```

The recovery of the sources is measured with the mean absolute correlation
coefficient (MCC):

```{r mcc, eval = tf_available()}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  method = c("iVAE", "GiVAE"),
  MCC = c(absolute_mean_correlation(fit_ivae$S, src$sources),
          absolute_mean_correlation(fit_givae$S, src$sources))
), digits = 3)
```

The estimated components are identified up to order and sign. After matching
each source with the estimated component it correlates with most, the true and
estimated sources of the first time point are

```{r compare, eval = tf_available(), fig.height = 5.5}
cors <- cor(fit_givae$S, src$sources)
ord <- apply(abs(cors), 2, which.max)
sgn <- sign(cors[cbind(ord, 1:3)])
first <- seq_len(n_area)
est <- sweep(fit_givae$S[first, ord, drop = FALSE], 2, sgn, "*")

plot_areal(src$sources[first, ], paste("Source", 1:3), "true")
plot_areal(est, paste("Estimate", 1:3), "estimated")
```

The nonstationary prior variances that identify the model are available from
`predict(fit_givae, type = "variance")`.

## Any graph, any layout

`GiVAE()` accepts one or several graphs, each described by `nlbss_graph()`:

* a graph with one node per observation (a general network), for example
  `GiVAE(x, graphs = nlbss_graph(W_n))` with an `n x n` matrix or adjacency list;
* a spatial graph and a time graph as above, or any other combination of
  graphs whose sizes divide the number of rows, using `each` for the layout;
* unsorted or incomplete data, where the node and the context of every row are
  given explicitly. Neighbours are looked up among the rows with the same
  context; rows that are missing simply have fewer neighbours.

As an example with the air pollution data (not run here), stations and days
form two graphs. The spatial graph connects every station to its four nearest
stations, and the rows can be in any order:

```{r pollution, eval = FALSE}
P <- pollution_northern_italy
station <- as.integer(factor(paste(P$Longitude, P$Latitude)))
day <- as.integer(factor(P$time))

st <- unique(data.frame(id = station, lon = P$Longitude, lat = P$Latitude))
st <- st[order(st$id), ]
D <- as.matrix(dist(st[, c("lon", "lat")]))
diag(D) <- Inf
nearest <- t(apply(D, 1, order))[, 1:4]
adj <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(nearest)), function(i) nearest[i, ])

g_station <- nlbss_graph(adj, node = station, context = day, name = "stations")
g_day <- nlbss_time_graph(max(day), node = day, context = station)

fit <- GiVAE(P, graphs = list(g_station, g_day), K = c(10, 10),
             vars = c("mean_O3", "mean_NO2", "mean_PM10"),
             latent_dim = 3, epochs = 100, batch_size = 64, seed = 1)
```
